summary: Markets traded narrowly lower Tuesday as geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz reignited after President Trump demanded compensation from Iran, stalling diplomatic progress and pushing oil back above $82. The Dow, S&P 500, and Nasdaq all dipped modestly, with tech giants Apple and Nvidia weighing on indices. Investors are now laser-focused on Wednesday's July CPI release, which is expected to show headline inflation rising 0.1% month-over-month and 3.4% year-over-year, a key input for the Fed's September rate decision. Crypto pulled back from recent highs, with Bitcoin falling 1.4% to open near $63,912 and Ethereum down 2% to $1,871, as institutional selling pressure resurfaced and traders braced for inflation data. In corporate news, Riot Platforms reportedly struck a $9 billion AI infrastructure deal with Anthropic, marking a dramatic pivot from bitcoin mining to artificial intelligence. Meanwhile, gold ETFs saw strong inflows and AbCellera Biologics surged nearly 40% on positive clinical trial results.

signals.title: Trump Demands Iran Compensation, Stalling Hormuz Deal
signals.desc: President Trump's demand for compensation from Iran derailed diplomatic talks to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, pushing oil prices back above $82 and dragging equities lower.

signals.title: July CPI Release Wednesday Morning at 8:30 AM ET
signals.desc: Markets await key July inflation data expected to show 3.4% year-over-year CPI, which could shift expectations for Fed rate moves in September.

signals.title: Bitcoin and Ethereum Retreat Ahead of CPI Data
signals.desc: Bitcoin opened down 1.4% at $63,912 and Ethereum fell 2% to $1,871 as institutional selling pressure and inflation uncertainty weighed on crypto sentiment.

signals.title: Riot Platforms Pivots to AI with $9B Anthropic Deal
signals.desc: Riot Platforms announced a reported $9 billion agreement with Anthropic to shift from bitcoin mining to AI infrastructure, underscoring crypto-to-AI sector rotation.

signals.title: Gold ETF Inflows Surge $626.8M on Safe-Haven Demand
signals.desc: The GLD ETF saw $626.8 million in inflows as shares outstanding rose 0.9%, reflecting demand for safe-haven assets amid geopolitical and inflation risks.

verdict: Markets are in wait-and-see mode ahead of Wednesday's CPI print, with geopolitical risk and inflation uncertainty capping risk appetite across equities and crypto.
